record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: If homomorphic encryption is used inside federated learning, who should hold the decryption key, and what trust structure or threshold-encryption design can preserve client privacy without assuming an unrealistic permanently trusted external decryptor?

evidence.quote: When considering the use of HE in the FL setting, questions immediately arise about who holds the secret key of the scheme. ... However, most HE schemes require that the secret keys be renewed often ... Moreover, the availability of a trusted non-colluding party is not standard in the FL setting.

artifact.category_tag: Threshold homomorphic encryption in federated learning
artifact.status_search_result: Numerous follow-up works propose threshold and multi-key HE schemes for federated aggregation (e.g., tMK-CKKS, distributed threshold additive HE with dropout resiliency, FedML-HE), distributing the decryption key among clients via secret sharing so that no single party (including the server) can decrypt individual updates. These address the trust issue under specific corruption thresholds and online/dropout assumptions, but no single solution has emerged that simultaneously handles cross-device churn, key rotation, and minimal trust assumptions optimally; recent critical analyses highlight remaining limitations. The broad open question of the right trust structure thus remains an active research area, with substantial partial progress.

status_evidence.title: A Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Scheme Using Threshold Multi-Key Homomorphic Encryption
status_evidence.snippet: tMK-CKKS: master public key shared by all clients; secret keys generated via linear secret sharing; decryption requires cooperation of t clients.
status_evidence.claim: Threshold multi-key HE removes the need for a single trusted decryptor by distributing the secret key among clients.

status_evidence.title: A Distributed Threshold Additive Homomorphic Encryption for Federated Learning with Dropout Resiliency
status_evidence.snippet: Lattice-based threshold HE scheme tolerating client dropouts in FL aggregation.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: threshold HE schemes designed specifically for federated learning with dropout.

status_evidence.title: A Critical Look into Threshold Homomorphic Encryption for Private Average Aggregation
status_evidence.snippet: Critical analysis of threshold HE in private average aggregation, identifying remaining trust and efficiency issues.
status_evidence.claim: Recent critical work indicates the problem is not fully resolved.
